definition: In linguistics and natural language processing, a corpus (pl.: corpora) or text corpus is a dataset, consisting of natively digital and older, digitalized, language resources, either annotated or unannotated.
details: Annotated, they have been used in corpus linguistics for statistical hypothesis testing, checking occurrences or validating linguistic rules within a specific language territory.

explainer.lead: A text corpus is a dataset of language resources, either natively digital or older digitized material, annotated or unannotated. It matters because corpora are the basis for corpus linguistics and natural language processing work.

tiers.eli5: It is a big organized collection of written text, like a library assembled specifically so a computer can study it.
tiers.practitioner: Annotated corpora are used for statistical hypothesis testing, checking occurrences, and validating linguistic rules within a specific language territory. The pitfall is forgetting that annotation choices shape what the corpus can validly test.
tiers.paperLevel: A corpus (plural corpora) or text corpus is a dataset consisting of natively digital and older digitized language resources, either annotated or unannotated; annotated corpora support statistical hypothesis testing and validation of linguistic rules.

explainer.example: A linguist queries an annotated corpus to check how often a construction occurs in a given language territory.
